title: HAL, Safran Sign Final Contract For Development Of 'Aravalli' Engine To Power India's 13-Tonne Military Helicopters
text:
Defence
Swarajya Staff
Aug 27, 2026 | Updated 09:42 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and France's Safran Helicopter Engines have signed a final contract with their joint venture SAFHAL Helicopter Engines for the development of a new-generation helicopter engine.
The Aravalli engine, rated at 3,500 to 4,000 shaft horsepower, will power HAL's upcoming 13-tonne Indian Multi-Role Helicopter and its naval variant, the Deck-Based Multi-Role Helicopter.
The agreement was signed in Bengaluru by Ajay Kumar Shrivastava, HAL's Director of Engineering, Research and Development, and Olivier Savin, Director of SAFHAL and Executive Vice President at Safran Helicopter Engines.
The engine derives its name from the ancient Aravalli mountain range in India. This marks the first time that a high-power helicopter engine is being designed and developed in India.
HAL and Safran will jointly develop the engine on a 50:50 basis, with SAFHAL manufacturing it at a facility in Tumakuru, Karnataka.
The design and development of the Aravalli engine is expected to be completed by 2032-33. The engine will power the helicopter that replaces India's long-serving Mi-17s.
The partnership provides HAL access to critical technologies, including a high-pressure compressor, power turbine, fuel and oil systems, accessory gearbox and external engine systems that will be crucial for developing future generations of indigenous aero-engines.
The Aravalli programme follows a lengthy timeline.
The partnership began with a memorandum of understanding in July 2022, followed by a workshare agreement in February 2023, the incorporation of SAFHAL in November 2023, and an airframer contract in August 2024, before reaching this final contract.
A separate HAL-Safran maintenance, repair and operations joint venture in Goa already supports TM333 and Shakti engines in Indian service.
